acceptance: Event remains UUIDv7 immutable revision 1, but Event ID and UUID lexical/time order have no event-order authority. One Event belongs to exactly one typed canonical owner stream.

A stream uses positive uint64 stream_seq beginning at 1, incrementing exactly by one for each accepted canonical append, and previous_event_id equals the immediately prior Event in that stream except for sequence 1 where it is absent. Duplicate sequence, gap, wrong predecessor, or conflicting Event ID fails closed.

Canonical per-stream ordering comes only from stream identity + stream_seq/predecessor. recorded_at/occurred_at are temporal observations, not authorization or ordering authority; separate streams have no implicit total ordering.

Event type uses a lowercase dotted provider-neutral grammar. Unknown/unnegotiated event type may be retained as opaque data only when compatibility policy later allows it, but cannot silently mutate a privileged canonical projection.
Event correlation can bind exact entity revisions plus RequestId/OperationId/GrantId and provenance Event IDs. These correlations are identifiers/evidence context, never authority tokens.
Corrections/supersession/forks create new Events; the prior Event is never mutated. Causal and lineage references are acyclic and do not replace stream order.

ArtifactRef binds canonical Artifact ID, exact revision when metadata matters, SHA-256 digest when bytes are relied on, role, and relevant media/size metadata. Digest mismatch is an explicit integrity failure.
Evidence is immutable revision 1. A changed claim, binding, observed result, qualifying input, limitation, or implementation revision requires a new Evidence ID.

Evidence records exact claim/subject bindings and source class. Agent/model self-report can explain intent but cannot satisfy a stronger independent gate. Machine/external/human-review evidence identifies the observation/artifact/event basis it actually checked.

Redaction/exclusion is explicit metadata. Redacted/exported views do not mutate canonical Event/Evidence; transformed bytes receive a new Artifact ID/digest; exclusions preserve that content was withheld and why, without storing secret plaintext in the manifest.
Large or sensitive payloads are referenced as Artifacts rather than duplicated into the Event envelope. Ordinary Event/Evidence records do not persist secret plaintext.

A projection can be rebuilt from canonical accepted Events, and a fixture can detect duplicate/gapped/out-of-order/wrong-predecessor stream entries, Artifact digest mismatch, cyclic causal lineage, in-place correction attempts, and evidence self-report masquerading as independent qualification.

Canonical docs remain consistent with IDENTITY_AND_REVISION_MODEL, RUNTIME_OPERATION_MODEL, ARCHITECTURE, QUALITY_AND_EVIDENCE, DATA_LIFECYCLE_AND_PORTABILITY, SECURITY_MODEL, and P01 registry without preempting S05.

Exact implementation passes focused stream-order, lineage-cycle, artifact-integrity, evidence-independence, redaction, and replay/projection adversarial checks plus pnpm check, git diff --check, Diffcipline R2, protected exact-head CI, and post-merge main qualification.

minimality.rationale: Freeze Event/Evidence semantics and one ADR in canonical documentation now; defer serialization, generated contracts, persistent storage, CAS implementation, export bundles, and compatibility fixtures to their dependency-ordered owners.

requirements: Never use Event UUID lexical order, producer timestamp, or controller receipt time as canonical stream-order authority.
Never mutate an existing Event or Evidence to correct history; append a new fact/assertion with explicit lineage.
Never let agent/model self-report satisfy a gate that requires independently observed machine, external, or human-review evidence.
Never silently omit/redact content from an exported or user-visible evidence view; preserve explicit exclusion/transformation metadata without secret plaintext.
Never treat Artifact ID alone as byte integrity when Evidence relies on bytes; bind and verify the content digest.

outcome: Kernux has one immutable, append-oriented, provider-neutral Event/Evidence contract with explicit stream ordering, request/operation/authority/provenance correlation, causal and fork lineage, exact Artifact references, independently qualified Evidence bindings, and redaction/exclusion metadata that preserves what was withheld without mutating history.
rationale: Identity, authorization, and runtime-operation semantics are PROVEN. P02 durable storage and later cross-language schemas need a stable Event/Evidence meaning before persistence or generated contracts are implemented; otherwise UUID/time ordering, mutable audit records, agent self-report, hidden payload loss, or redaction could corrupt replay and proof.

risk.recovery: Revert the Event/Evidence semantic contract, ADR, aligned docs, and closeout state. No persistent event store or production evidence bundle exists yet, so this task requires no stored-data migration.

scope_in: Define an immutable conceptual v1 Event envelope using canonical Event UUIDv7 identity/revision 1, exact event_type, stream identity, explicit stream sequence, previous-event linkage, producer identity, occurred/recorded time roles, exact entity/runtime/request/operation/Grant correlations, causal references, payload/artifact references, sensitivity/redaction metadata, and schema/event-contract version metadata.

Define a provider-neutral lowercase dotted event-type grammar and core namespace ownership without requiring every future event type to be enumerated in this task. Unknown/unnegotiated event types cannot silently drive privileged projections.

Define canonical stream semantics without introducing a new core Stream entity: one Event belongs to exactly one typed owner stream over a canonical Project, Task, Run, or Runtime identity. Define positive uint64 stream_seq assigned by durable canonical append authority and exact previous_event_id chaining.

Define ordering rules: stream_seq/previous_event_id own canonical per-stream order; Event UUIDv7 lexical order and timestamps are not ordering authority; different streams have no implied total order unless explicit causal links establish relationships.

Define append/correction behavior: Event is immutable; correction/supersession is a new Event linked to the prior Event; projection state is rebuilt from durable Events and cannot mutate history to make a timeline look cleaner.

Define event correlation with exact Project/Task/WorkUnit/Run/AgentSession/Runtime revisions where relevant plus RequestId, OperationId, GrantId, source Event IDs, and producer component/Runtime/AgentSession identity without treating those references as authority.

Define causal/lineage semantics for caused_by, supersedes, forked_from/checkpoint relationships with acyclic lineage requirements and explicit statement that causal links do not replace stream ordering.

Define Artifact references as exact Artifact ID/revision plus SHA-256 content digest when bytes matter, media type/size metadata where known, role, and source Event linkage. Large/sensitive payloads move to Artifact storage rather than being duplicated into Event records.

Define Evidence as immutable revision-1 assertion with exact claim/subject bindings, observer/source class, observed Event references, relevant Artifact exact refs/digests, runtime/operation/provider-adapter version context, result/outcome, limitations, and qualifying implementation revision where applicable.

Define evidence independence: agent/model self-report may be recorded but cannot satisfy a machine/external/human-independent gate that requires stronger evidence; Evidence must say what source class established the claim.

Define redaction/exclusion metadata for durable records and exported views: none|excluded|transformed plus reason/policy/version and affected field/artifact roles. Redaction never mutates the original Event/Evidence; transformed bytes are a new Artifact; omission is represented explicitly in manifests/views.

Define secret-minimization rules: ordinary Event/Evidence records store secret references/classification, not secret plaintext; hashes/digests are not automatically non-sensitive; payload placement/export remains policy-bound.

Define replay/projection integrity invariants including monotonic contiguous per-stream sequencing, predecessor linkage, duplicate Event ID rejection, sequence conflict rejection, missing-link detection, immutable facts, and projection rebuild from canonical events.

Add an accepted ADR and align ARCHITECTURE, QUALITY_AND_EVIDENCE, DATA_LIFECYCLE_AND_PORTABILITY, RUNTIME_OPERATION_MODEL, and identity downstream requirements without selecting wire schema or persistence layout.
scope_out: Do not choose JSON Schema/Protobuf/other single schema source or generate Rust/TypeScript types; S05-T01 owns this.
Do not define global additive/unknown-field compatibility behavior; S05-T02 owns this.
Do not build the executable protocol fixture corpus; S05-T03 owns this.
Do not implement SQLite/event store, CAS, projections, export bundle, encryption, retention engine, or runtime event transport; later phases own those implementations.
Do not define canonical Event byte digest before S05 freezes canonical serialization; Artifact byte digest remains SHA-256 as already proven.
title: KX-P01-S04-T01 — Freeze Event envelope, lineage, artifact, evidence, and redaction semantics
